summary: Monolith ASP.NET Core on Azure App Service with Azure SQL Database as the database in India; front end: Blazor.

frontend.justification: Lets a C# team build the UI without switching to JavaScript. Fit for this project: team.languages includes C#; well suited to internal tool projects; strong maintainability for Blazor (priority 5); strong time to market for Blazor (priority 5).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 0.2 points lower: the chosen option wins on priorities.security (strong security for Blazor (priority 4)).
Scored 1.3 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).

tradeoffs: Smaller UI component ecosystem than React.
WebAssembly mode has a heavy first load; Server mode needs a live connection.

backend.justification: High-performance C# with first-class Entra ID and SignalR support. Fit for this project: team.languages includes C#; first-class Microsoft Entra ID integration; strong maintainability for ASP.NET Core (priority 5); well suited to internal tool projects.

alternatives.why_not: Scored 4.8 points lower: the chosen option wins on infrastructure.existing_systems (first-class Microsoft Entra ID integration).
Scored 5.7 points lower: the chosen option wins on infrastructure.existing_systems (first-class Microsoft Entra ID integration).

alternatives.choice: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage + Realtime + Edge Functions)
alternatives.why_not: Excluded: Supabase is not on AZURE, and cloud_preference=azure is a hard constraint (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Best tooling assumes the Microsoft ecosystem.

database.justification: Reuses existing SQL Server skills, schemas and tooling. Fit for this project: reuses the existing SQL Server / Azure SQL Database data and skills; strong security for SQL Server / Azure SQL Database (priority 4); strong maintainability for SQL Server / Azure SQL Database (priority 5); strong time to market for SQL Server / Azure SQL Database (priority 5). Data stays in Central India (Pune) to satisfy data_residency=india.

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server (Central India (Pune))
alternatives.why_not: Scored 2.4 points lower: the chosen option wins on infrastructure.existing_systems (reuses the existing SQL Server / Azure SQL Database data and skills).

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server (Central India (Pune))
alternatives.why_not: Scored 4.2 points lower: the chosen option wins on infrastructure.existing_systems (reuses the existing SQL Server / Azure SQL Database data and skills).
Excluded: Google Cloud is not on AZURE, and cloud_preference=azure is a hard constraint (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Licensing makes self-hosted or non-Azure deployments expensive.

hosting.justification: Managed web hosting with built-in Entra ID sign-in, slots and VNet integration. Fit for this project: strong time to market for Azure App Service (priority 5); well suited to internal tool projects; built-in Entra ID sign-in (Easy Auth).

alternatives.why_not: Scored 8.6 points lower: the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).
Scored 3.7 points lower: operational burden (ops 2/5) with no DevOps engineer; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to internal tool projects).
Excluded: DigitalOcean is not on AZURE, and cloud_preference=azure is a hard constraint (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Per-instance pricing does not scale to zero.

supporting.justification: Employees already sign in with Entra ID; the app trusts it via OpenID Connect, so there are no new passwords and joiners/leavers are handled centrally. App Service 'Easy Auth' can enforce sign-in with no auth code.

alternatives.why_not: Would duplicate the identity provider the company already runs.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Clients upload directly with pre-signed URLs, so large files never pass through the API; objects are encrypted at rest and private by default.

alternatives.why_not: Fine for documents, poor as app storage.

tradeoffs: Needs lifecycle rules to control growth.

supporting.justification: Caches static assets and public media close to users and absorbs traffic spikes.

alternatives.why_not: Slower first loads for public pages and media.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (payment webhooks, notifications, image processing, scoring) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.justification: Listed in existing_systems; integrate through its official API with a service account and least-privilege scopes rather than duplicating its data.

supporting.choice: Azure Key Vault + Activity Log + Azure WAF
supporting.justification: Compliance controls for ISO27001: encryption keys you control, no secrets in code, tamper-evident audit logs and a web application firewall.

alternatives.why_not: Auditors expect platform-level key management and logs.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights + OpenTelemetry tracing
supporting.justification: Logs, metrics and traces stay in the same cloud and region as the data; Sentry has no India data region.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L2: ~1500 users, ~300 peak concurrent, ~60 req/s at peak, ~20 GB stored
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees, SMS and payment-gateway transaction fees

warnings.message: Existing system 'On-prem SQL Server 2019': Mainstream support ended 28 Feb 2025; extended (security-only) support runs to 8 Jan 2030. Plan an upgrade or migrate to Azure SQL Database. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/products/sql-server-2019

Existing system 'Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)': Azure AD is now Microsoft Entra ID; same service, new name. Integrate via OIDC/SAML. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/new-name
Upper estimate ($616) exceeds the $300 budget; watch usage as you grow.

An existing SQL Server is listed: migrate the relevant tables to the managed database (Azure Database Migration Service / DMS) or reach the on-prem server through a private connection; do not expose it publicly.
